title: Mixed madd practice: which madd is it?: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-Fajr and the families of madd
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 26 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Mixed madd practice rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 26. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

keywords.def: madd letter and hamza in the same word: 4 or 5 counts
madd letter at the end of a word, hamza at the start of the next: 4 or 5 counts

questions.q: Label each madd in «وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ» (90:12).
questions.a: وَمَآ: munfasil (4); أَدْرَىٰكَ: natural (2); مَا: natural (2).

questions.q: A madd with no hamza or sukoon after it is ...
Madd map (pupil PDF): colour natural madds green and muttasil/munfasil red in Al-Balad 90:1 to 12. Today's rota group recites Al-Fajr 89:1 to 6.
questions.a: Red: لَآ (90:1), يَرَهُۥٓ (90:7), وَمَآ (90:12); the others are green.

questions.q: Extend: write one example of each madd from any surah you know.
questions.a: For example: مَالًۭا natural, جَآءَ muttasil, لَآ أُقْسِمُ munfasil.

questions.q: Stretch: why must muttasil be stretched, while munfasil may be shortened?
questions.a: In muttasil the hamza is always there; in munfasil the hamza belongs to the next word, and in some readings it is shortened.
A) Muttasil. The hamza is in the same word as the alif: muttasil.

questions.q: Think again: If you had to explain the three madds to a younger brother or sister in one sentence each, what would you say?
questions.a: Natural: just stretch 2. Joined: hamza in the same word, 4. Separated: hamza in the next word, 4.
